# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Pass 20** — through-code on Datasec/NexusAI S29's GUARD + DOC round at `5a7c6b5` against `7e5faa9` (2026-09-04 03:45→04:06; static, no browser, zero writes to the NexusAI tree, blast radius established BEFORE anything was run): **PASS with findings — 3 Major / 3 Minor; the load-bearing claim CONFIRMED and confirmed harder than it was stated** | 1 | 1.0 | 1.0 | Wednesday read the FULL 36,663-byte report, not the summary mail. The keepers: **it verified the zero-rendered-pixel claim with TWO independent parsers, each individually red-proofed** — a CSS Syntax L3 tokenizer and the CSSOM AST already vendored in the tree — and **red-proofed both four ways** (a single hex digit changed, a comment closed early so a declaration leaks live, `*/` inside a string correctly ignored, an unterminated comment reported loudly rather than swallowed); **it extended the claim to `derive-brand-tokens.js` unprompted** because that file WRITES `tokens.css`, so a behavioural change there moves pixels on the next regeneration even though today's output is byte-identical; **it ran the gate at BOTH SHAs from scratchpad copies rather than inheriting the baseline** (1399/82 and 1395/81, the +4/+1 reconciling exactly to the new suite run alone); **F-2 is the finding of the pass** — it inserted the guard's OWN negative-control wording verbatim into a 9,233-character dated comment block and **the suite stayed fully green**, then measured paragraph widths across all seven scanned files to show `paragraphAt()`'s `\n\n` delimiter makes a whole `/* … */` block one paragraph, **up to 10,367 characters, in the four comment-shaped files where three of the four original wrong sentences lived**; **F-1 was proven by a disable-one-family-at-a-time table run against the REAL suite**, showing `f-fixed-prose` isolates nothing and `DATED` has no pass-side control at all; **F-3 is arithmetic against the document's own stated population** — BRAND.md says *"The other nine clear it"* where seven is right. **Its blast-radius section is a model**: it established the test ports band at 39000+ cannot collide with the live 3068–3077 surfaces, that the generator's only write is skipped under `--stdout`, and that `HOME` is repointed by the suite's own containment helper — **before running anything**. **And its self-correction is the most useful thing in it: its first corpus sweep reported a confident ZERO because an unquoted shell variable handed its scanner an empty file list** — caught only because it refused to accept a zero while it could see the co-occurrence with its own eyes; correct figure 12, published with the reasoning error named as *"the failure the guard's own POSITIVE CONTROL exists to prevent, committed by the person auditing it."* **The closing line is now a fleet standing insight: "each round's red-proof is built in the shape of the LAST round's bug, so each new guard is strongest exactly where the previous failure was and untested where the next one will be."** |
| Datasec/NexusAI agent | S29 — the GUARD + DOC round at `5a7c6b5` (the seven-item queue Wednesday set after pass 19; wrapped at `11cdf5a`, HISTORY.md only): **the load-bearing promise KEPT — not one rendered pixel moved, and the gate proved it with two independent red-proofed parsers — but the guard built to end a four-times-recurring count error carries two of the three shapes this project keeps reproducing, and the corrected paragraph shipped a fresh count error** | 1 | 0.80 | 0.80 | Scored after pass 20 + Wednesday's completion check. Credits: **the zero-pixel claim
